rows.title: Generic lifecycle exists as library APIs
rows.evidence: Iteration 2 (delta F3): crates/nono/src/lifecycle/ landed with pure typed state machine (10 states x 11 ops, exhaustive matrix test, single-use + stop-blocks-activation + one-death-one-fact refusals test-locked), SandboxPlan/ValidatedPlan typestate with full pre-launch validation (secrets-redacting Debug), EventSink trait with Observation fidelity labels. 45 unit + 2 doc tests. Pending: prepare/activate/wait/stop/cleanup-verify OS-backed APIs (ADR-0001 sections 3-6). || Iteration 11 (final): PASS. Every lifecycle operation the contract names exists as a LIBRARY API in crates/nono, reachable without a process boundary and without the CLI (R14 is the standing guard for the second half of that claim). Audited against crates/nono/src/lib.rs:100-114 (crate-root re-exports) and crates/nono/src/lifecycle/mod.rs:124-164 (module re-exports). PLAN -> nono::lifecycle::{SandboxPlan, ValidatedPlan, PlanError, GateConfig, SessionMode, ResourceLimits, MAX_PLAN_METADATA_BYTES}; SandboxPlan::validate() is the typestate boundary. PREPARE -> PreparedSandbox::prepare(ValidatedPlan) -> (PreparedSandbox, ActivationHandle); SessionStore::prepare(plan) for the durable variant; SessionStore::prepare_detached(plan) -> (DetachedSession, ActivationHandle); PrepareError. ACTIVATE -> PreparedSandbox::activate(&ActivationHandle) -> ActivatedSandbox; DetachedSession::activate; AttachedTerminal::activate; ActivationHandle::{from_parts, token}; ActivationError; ACTIVATION_TOKEN_BYTES. WAIT -> ActivatedSandbox::{wait, try_wait} -> SandboxExit; DetachedSession::wait -> WaitOutcome::{Exit, StillRunning}. EXIT FACTS -> SandboxExit, ExitOutcome, ActivationObservation, PreExecStage, SupervisorStage, ReapError, PRE_EXEC_EXIT_CODE. STOP -> ActivatedSandbox::stop, PreparedSandbox::stop_before_activation, DetachedSession::stop, StopError. CLEANUP VERIFY -> ActivatedSandbox::verify_cleanup, PreparedSandbox::verify_cleanup, RecoveredSession::{verify_cleanup, verify_cleanup_by}, DetachedSession::verify_cleanup; CleanupVerification, AbsenceBasis, SurvivorEvidence, IndeterminateReason, UnsupportedReason, CleanupError. STATE -> LifecycleState, LifecycleOp, TransitionError. SESSIONS/RECOVERY -> SessionStore::{open, prepare, prepare_detached, sessions, recover, attach_control, control_socket_path}, SessionRecord, SessionSummary, Sessions, RecoveredSession::{attach, supervisor, kill_group, kill_pid}, RecoveryDecision, SupervisorPresence, reconcile, SessionStoreError, CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION, OLDEST_SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION, MAX_RECORD_BYTES. DETACHED/CONTROL -> supervisor_entry, DetachedSession::{status, detach, supervisor, opened_in}, SessionStatus, ControlRequest, ControlReply, ControlRefusal, FrameError, CONTROL_PROTOCOL_VERSION, CONTROL_TIMEOUT, MAX_CONTROL_WAIT, MAX_CONTROL_FRAME_BYTES, DetachedError, DETACHED_EVENT_RING_CAPACITY. TERMINAL/ATTACH -> DetachedSession::attach(WindowSize) -> AttachedTerminal::{write_input, resize, ping, read_event, activate, detach, ack, session_id, supervisor}, TerminalEvent, TerminalEnd, AttachAck, AttachError, AttachViolation, AttachTag, Peer, MAX_ATTACH_PAYLOAD_BYTES, SCROLLBACK_CAPACITY_BYTES. IDENTITY -> ProcessIdentity. EVENTS -> EventSink, LifecycleEvent, LifecycleEventKind, ActivationOutcome, Observation. SUPPORT -> SupportReport::gather(), lifecycle::Capability, SupportStatus, Determination, SupportReason, HostFacts, KernelFacts, LandlockFacts, LandlockRight, LandlockRightSupport, NetworkFilteringFacts, NetworkMechanism, NetworkMechanismSupport, IdentityFacts, CleanupFacts, EventObservationSupport, EventFamily, EventFidelity, DarkSpot, DarkSpotEntry, SUPPORT_REPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION. CAPABILITY MODES -> FsMode, FsModeSet, FsModeCapability, CompiledModes, ModeBundle, ModeRefusal, ModeAlwaysAllowed, ModeDelegation, ModeEnforceability, BundleReason, RefusalReason, AlwaysAllowedReason, DelegationTarget, ModeTarget, CapabilitySet::{allow_path_modes, allow_file_modes, fs_mode_capabilities, add_fs_modes}, Sandbox::compile_fs_modes. ERRORS -> LifecycleError aggregate reached through NonoError::Lifecycle, with a diagnostic_code arm per variant. Two omissions are deliberate and documented at lib.rs:93-99: lifecycle::ResourceLimits is module-only (it would collide with resource::ResourceLimits, a different concept) and lifecycle::Capability is module-only (at the crate root it would read as a peer of CapabilitySet). lifecycle::{Sessions, reconcile} are likewise module-only. This row is host-independent: it asks whether the APIs EXIST, and they compile and are exercised on this host. The question of whether their Linux arms BEHAVE is R03/R04/R06/R07/R09/R10/R11, which are BLOCKED.

rows.title: Stop/activate/wait races tested
rows.evidence: Iteration 4 (delta F5): SharedLifecycle sync core (single lock owns LifecycleState + three-valued GateEffect; every mutation via LifecycleState::apply; CAS+release one critical section). 5 Loom models exhaust interleavings: two activations -> one winner/one release; activate-vs-stop never both-win-and-release; death-vs-stop one fact; no release after SupervisorLost; duplicate cleanup one winner. Harness detects deliberately weakened CAS (3/5 models fail). Gate: RUSTFLAGS=--cfg nono_loom cargo test -p nono --test loom_lifecycle --release. Iteration 6 (delta F7) added scenario 6, so the R05 model set is complete: 7 Loom models. The two new ones cover the durable store's own race - a recovery reconciling a record while another party confirms the same cleanup (exactly one CleanupConfirmed winner; a recovery that observes the cleanup already proven records nothing) and a recovery racing a stop-then-cleanup (never adopt after cleanup). The recovery's read-decide-record is deliberately not one critical section - reconcile() is pure over an already-read state - and these models are what say that gap is safe. || Iteration 11 (final): PASS, and the judgement differs from the sibling Linux-blocked rows for a reason worth stating. This row's contract scope is a DETERMINISTIC HARNESS for the race scenarios, and loom is host-independent by construction: it is a model checker that replaces std's atomics, cells and locks with instrumented ones and enumerates interleavings inside one process. It performs no syscall, forks nothing, touches no kernel interface, and reaches no platform-specific code — every model drives lifecycle::sync_core, which is pure synchronisation over LifecycleState::apply. A Linux runner would execute the same enumeration and reach the same verdict; there is no 'Linux half' of this row to be missing, which is exactly why it is PASS while R03/R04/R09/R10/R11 are BLOCKED. Gate: loom-lifecycle in scripts/stream-gates.sh (RUSTFLAGS='--cfg nono_loom' cargo test -p nono --test loom_lifecycle --release) = 7 passed / 0 failed. The seven models cover the six contract scenarios plus the recovery pair: two activations -> one winner and one release; activate-vs-stop -> never both, and no release after a stop wins; child-death-vs-stop -> one death records one fact; supervisor-loss-vs-activate -> no release after Failed; duplicate cleanup -> one winner; recovery-vs-cleanup -> exactly one CleanupConfirmed winner; recovery-vs-stop-then-cleanup -> never adopt after cleanup. The harness is verified to DETECT a deliberately weakened (non-atomic read-then-write) CAS: 3 of 5 models failed on the weakened build. The cfg is nono_loom rather than loom's own name because RUSTFLAGS reaches every crate and --cfg loom makes tokio compile out tokio::net, which hyper-util (transitive via sigstore-verify) then fails to find; build.rs declares it via cargo::rustc-check-cfg so unexpected_cfgs still catches real typos.

rows.title: Machine-readable support report
rows.evidence: Iteration 7 (delta F8) landed lifecycle/support.rs. SupportReport::gather() is infallible and returns a tree of Capability<T> = {status: available|partial|unavailable|unknown, determination: probed_live|platform_api|declared, reason: typed (probed | probe_refused | other_platform | platform_api_linked | not_implemented | not_observable_without_irreversible_change | platform_cannot_express), facts: typed or absent}. NO BARE BOOLEAN anywhere in the serialized tree, locked structurally by a test that walks serde_json::Value and rejects Value::Bool at any depth (removal-detected: adding one bool to CleanupFacts fails 3 tests and prints the JSON pointer). Fields: host (compiled target AND uname(2) sysname/release/version/machine; node name deliberately not read - a hostname is not a capability fact), landlock (REUSES upstream Sandbox::detect_abi + DetectedAbi::has_* for a per-right table filesystem_base/refer/truncate/execute/tcp_network/ioctl_dev/scoping - available only if every right is, else partial; zero diff to sandbox/*), seccomp (upstream's own fork-isolated probe_seccomp_block_network_support -> probed_live), seccomp_user_notification (honestly UNKNOWN: SECCOMP_FILTER_FLAG_NEW_LISTENER cannot be established without installing a filter that cannot be removed from the installing process, and a kernel release number is not proof since CONFIG_SECCOMP_FILTER can be off), seatbelt (PLATFORM_API not probed_live, with the rationale in reason.why_not_probed: sandbox_init is linked so presence is a compile-time fact, but it applies process-wide and irreversibly, so a live probe must fork - the CLI's setup --check-only does exactly that and is not library machinery; asserted by a macOS test), network_filtering (per-mechanism table incl. seatbelt_per_port_tcp = unavailable/platform_cannot_express naming NetworkFilterUnsupported, so the absence is STATED not inferred), pty (live posix_openpt(O_RDWR|O_NOCTTY) closed immediately -> probed_live) kept SEPARATE from interactive_session (not_implemented) so 'pty: available' cannot be misread as 'the lifecycle will give you one', detached_supervisor + attach (unavailable/not_implemented{R09 slice B} - honest, slice B pending), process_identity (captures THIS process and re-checks: start_time/boot_id/self_recognition all probed_live true on this host), cleanup_verification (signal-0 probes of self and own group, reusing cleanup::{probe_pid,probe_group} made pub(crate) so the report cannot drift from the mechanism), event_observation (per-family fidelity map; kernel_denial = NOT_OBSERVED on BOTH platforms - the lifecycle installs no seccomp-notify listener and macOS Seatbelt denials reach userspace only via the system log; the CLI's log-stream reconstruction is explicitly NOT claimed), dark_spots (typed list of the 4 limits already recorded in module docs: setsid group escape, pgid reuse after reap, exec-or-killed EOF ambiguity, Instant-frozen gate expiry - each with consequence + the file that documents it). Upstream SupportInfo{is_supported} untouched. 17 unit tests + docs/lifecycle/support-report-v1.md with a golden example locked by a snapshot test that reads the doc itself. macOS values live-verified; the Linux halves (landlock ABI table, seccomp probe) are written-unverified behind the R07 Docker blocker. || Iteration 8 (F9) updated two entries: detached_supervisor Unavailable/NotImplemented -> Available/PlatformApi with the supervisor_entry() precondition and its typed failure named in reason.why_not_probed (a probe would have to launch a supervisor); attach Unavailable -> Partial, because control attach landed and terminal attach did not. Both are asserted by their own tests and both are in the golden example locked by docs/lifecycle/support-report-v1.md. || Iteration 9 (F10) updated two more entries: interactive_session Unavailable/NotImplemented -> Available/PlatformApi, and attach Partial -> Available/PlatformApi. NEITHER became probed_live, and the distinction was kept deliberately: interactive_session takes its STATUS from the live posix_openpt probe (a host that will not give this process a pseudo-terminal cannot run an interactive session however good the supervisor is, and the refusal is then reported with the probe's own reason and its probed_live strength) but NOT its DETERMINATION, because the supervisor half cannot be established without forking twice, execing this binary again, binding a socket and writing a durable record. The live suite tests/lifecycle_detached.rs drives the whole path, but a test that ran on somebody else's machine is not a probe that ran in this process during this call, and probed_live means the latter - claiming it would make the strongest word in this module mean something weaker. attach's why_not_probed states the three limits a consumer must plan around: attach occupies the supervisor's single client slot (a second connection is refused ControlRefusal::Busy), a headless run has no terminal (ControlRefusal::NoTerminal), and scrollback is a bounded ring whose dropped-byte count rides on the next AttachAck. Both entries are asserted by their own tests and both are in the golden example locked by docs/lifecycle/support-report-v1.md. || Iteration 11 (final): PASS. The row asks for a machine-readable support report, and the deliverable is the machinery plus its honesty guarantees, both of which are verified here and are host-independent in the way that matters: NO BARE BOOLEAN can appear anywhere in the serialized tree, and that is locked STRUCTURALLY by a test that walks serde_json::Value and rejects Value::Bool at any depth (removal-detected: adding one bool field to CleanupFacts fails 3 tests and names the JSON pointer). Every field is a Capability<T> carrying status / determination / typed reason / optional typed facts, so 'I do not know' and 'the platform cannot express this' are distinct answers rather than one false. The report tells the truth about itself on THIS host and would tell a different truth on Linux by construction, which is the point: seatbelt is platform_api and NOT probed_live because sandbox_init is irreversible and process-wide; seccomp_user_notification is honestly unknown because establishing SECCOMP_FILTER_FLAG_NEW_LISTENER means installing a filter that cannot be removed; interactive_session and attach are available/platform_api rather than probed_live because the supervisor half cannot be established without forking twice and execing this binary — and a test that ran on somebody else's machine is not a probe that ran in this process during this call. Gate: the report's 20 unit tests and its golden-example snapshot (which reads docs/lifecycle/support-report-v1.md through include_str!, so doc drift fails the build) are inside the nono-crate-tests gate = 1145 passed / 0 failed. See the note for the Linux gathering.

rows.title: Generic event delivery for directly observed events
rows.evidence: Iteration 7 (delta F8) expanded lifecycle/events.rs to the contract shape. LifecycleEvent is now an envelope {session_id: Option<Uuid> (always Some in practice), generation, seq: u64, observed_at: SystemTime captured AT observation, identity: Option<ProcessIdentity>, observation: Observation} around a closed what: LifecycleEventKind {StateChanged (kept, so existing consumers keep their fact), PrepareStarted, SandboxApplied, GateReady, ActivationAttempted{outcome}, Released, ExecObserved, ChildExited{outcome}, StopRequested, StopObserved{outcome}, GateAborted, SupervisorFailure{stage,errno}, CleanupVerdict{verdict}, RecordPersisted{schema_version}}. seq is owned by a crate-internal EventEmitter shared by Arc across the prepared->activated handoff, so one run is ONE unbroken sequence (removal-detected: a second emitter restarts at 0 mid-run and fails both live sequence tests); seq is documented as the ordering authority and observed_at explicitly is NOT (a wall clock can step). ActivationOutcome = {Accepted, RefusedWrongSession, RefusedWrongGeneration, RefusedGateClosed{state}, RefusedExpired, RefusedInvalidToken} carries NO token material by construction, locked by a test that walks the serialized tree rejecting any key named token/nonce/secret/digest and ANY array (every secret in the module is a [u8; N]) plus a long-blob check over serde and Debug (removal-detected). No synthesized kernel denials: the vocabulary has no variant for what the platform does not show. Emission points: prepare() -> PrepareStarted (pre-fork, the one event with no identity); the child's gate-ready record -> SandboxApplied + GateReady; activate() -> ActivationAttempted at every outcome, Released after the claim's write, ExecObserved on EOF; wait() -> ChildExited; stop paths -> StopRequested/StopObserved; abort_gate -> GateAborted (only when a live gate was closed); fail_activation -> SupervisorFailure; verify_cleanup -> CleanupVerdict for EVERY verdict, not only ConfirmedAbsent; SessionStore write -> RecordPersisted (never for a write that failed). Every emit is outside the SharedLifecycle lock and after the fact; SessionHandle::persist was restructured to release the record mutex BEFORE calling the sink, so consumer code never runs under a library lock. Rule the order follows: the fact first, then the state change it caused. Proven: 8 new unit tests + 3 live (whole-vocabulary happy run, stopped run reported as stop_requested/stop_observed rather than child_exited, refused activation carrying no token material), each live test asserting the exact sequence, seq gaplessness, observed_at non-decreasing, and identity present on every event after the fork. docs/lifecycle/lifecycle-event-v1.md carries the field table and a golden example locked by a snapshot test. macOS live-verified; the Linux halves are the same code paths behind the R07 blocker. || Iteration 8 (F9) added the honest answer to 'what happens to events when there is no caller'. EventSink stays caller-side and NOTHING was invented to deliver events to a caller that is not there: a detached supervisor installs its own EventRing sink and persists the last DETACHED_EVENT_RING_CAPACITY = 32 events into the session record (schema v2 field), oldest dropped, read back by DetachedSession::status().events(). The fidelity is documented as bounded and lossy in three places (the constant, the record schema doc, and the client module). The one event a supervisor learns about rather than witnesses - a child that ended at the gate while nobody asked - is emitted with Observation::Reconstructed, as is the PrepareStarted of an adopted child, whose fork happened in the launcher before the supervisor image existed. || Iteration 11 (final): PASS. The row asks for generic event delivery for DIRECTLY OBSERVED events, and the load-bearing guarantee is a negative one that is verified here and cannot vary by host: THE VOCABULARY HAS NO VARIANT FOR WHAT THE PLATFORM DOES NOT SHOW. There is no kernel-denial event to synthesize a reconstruction into, on either platform, and event_observation reports kernel_denial as not_observed on BOTH — the CLI's macOS log-stream reconstruction is explicitly not claimed as library machinery. The two places a supervisor LEARNS rather than WITNESSES (a child that ended at the gate while nobody asked; the PrepareStarted of an adopted child, whose fork happened in the launcher before the supervisor image existed) are labelled Observation::Reconstructed. seq is the documented ordering authority and observed_at explicitly is not, because a wall clock can step; seq is owned by one Arc-shared EventEmitter across the prepared->activated handoff, removal-detected (a second emitter restarts at 0 mid-run and fails both live sequence tests, left: 0 right: 9). ActivationOutcome carries no token material BY CONSTRUCTION, locked by a test that walks the serialized tree rejecting any key named token/nonce/secret/digest and ANY array (every secret in the module is a [u8; N], so an array is the shape a leak would take), plus a long-blob check over serde AND Debug. Every emit is outside the SharedLifecycle lock and after the fact, and SessionHandle::persist releases the record mutex BEFORE calling the sink, so consumer code never runs under a library lock. The honest answer to 'what happens with no caller' is a bounded lossy ring (32 events) in the record, documented as bounded and lossy in three places rather than presented as delivery. Gate: the events unit tests plus 3 live sequence tests are inside nono-crate-tests (1145/0) and lifecycle-live (25/0); the golden example in docs/lifecycle/lifecycle-event-v1.md is snapshot-locked. Linux emission runs the same code paths and will be exercised by the ubuntu-latest CI job.
rows.note: API shape change for consumers: LifecycleEvent went from enum to struct. LifecycleEvent::StateChanged{from,to,observation} is now LifecycleEventKind::StateChanged{from,to} reached via event.what(), with observation on the envelope. Recorded in HANDOFF.md.

rows.title: No Nono CLI invocation required by library consumers
rows.evidence: True at baseline (crates/nono is a leaf; no CLI subprocess calls). At risk until R02 lands in crates/nono rather than nono-cli; re-verify each iteration (grep gate: Command::new("nono")|CARGO_BIN_EXE_nono in crates/nono/src must stay empty). || Iteration 11 (final): PASS, grep gate run and EMPTY. Command and result verbatim: `grep -rnE 'Command::new\("nono"\)|CARGO_BIN_EXE_nono' crates/nono/src` -> no output, exit 1 (grep's no-match status). Zero hits at any depth of the library source tree. The claim is stronger than the grep, and the grep is only the tripwire: crates/nono has no dependency on crates/nono-cli (it is a leaf in the workspace graph), so a CLI invocation could not be reached even indirectly. The one place the library re-executes a binary is the detached supervisor, and what it re-executes is std::env::current_exe() — THE CONSUMER'S OWN BINARY, recognised by the supervisor_entry() hook — never a nono binary and never a looked-up path, which is deliberate: a path is something an attacker can arrange to control. Re-run this gate at every iteration; it is one line and it is the only thing standing between the library and a hidden process dependency.

rows.title: No CrystalOS/HCP/Leash-policy/Cedar type in fork
rows.evidence: Grep-confirmed at baseline: RuntimeProvider/LaunchRequest/PolicyBundle/SandboxEvent/Cedar/HCP exist only in the consumer repo. Guard: re-grep the fork for these tokens at every iteration gate. || Iteration 11 (final): PASS, re-grepped case-sensitively across the full scope. Command: `grep -rnE 'RuntimeProvider|LaunchRequest|PolicyBundle|SandboxEvent|Cedar|HCP|CrystalOS|Leash' crates/nono/src docs/lifecycle docs/adr`. crates/nono/src: ZERO hits — no product type, no product concept, not even in a comment. docs/lifecycle: ZERO hits. docs/adr: exactly ONE hit, docs/adr/0001-generic-lifecycle.md:17, reading 'all generic (no CrystalOS/HCP/Leash/Cedar concepts)'. JUSTIFICATION: it is the NEGATIVE statement — the sentence that declares the boundary this row exists to enforce. Removing it would make the grep cleaner and the repository less honest. It is prose in a design record, not a type, not an identifier, and not reachable by any compiler. Counting it as a violation would mean the boundary can be documented only by not naming what is on the other side of it. No other hit exists anywhere in scope, including substring hits — checked, and there are none to justify. R14 and R15 together are the two standing tripwires; both are one-line commands and both must be re-run at every iteration gate.
